This avoids working-capital accrual changes and does not recycle the fixed-charge-and-maturity rehabilitation core.

considered.name: Post-Gross Cost Creep Under Accumulated Loss
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), oiadp), revt), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms earn lower subsequent returns when costs below gross profit consume an increasing share of revenue and retained earnings are depleted.
considered.reasoning: The first leg measures deterioration in gross-to-operating conversion rather than inverse gross profitability, supplier claims, or a static SG&A level. Accumulated losses identify firms with limited capacity to absorb rising overhead, depreciation, and other post-gross operating costs.

considered.name: Capital-Base Productivity Decline with Liability Growth
considered.hypothesis: Firms earn lower subsequent returns when revenue generated per unit of depreciation declines while current liabilities grow.
considered.reasoning: The profitability channel is a deterioration in capital-base productivity rather than the level of depreciation, gross profit, or capital-consumption coverage. Growing current liabilities make that deterioration financially consequential by increasing near-term claims as productive capacity weakens.

considered.name: Financing-Cost Mix Shift Under Cash Scarcity
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(xint, ADD(xint, ADD(cogs, xsga))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, act))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms earn lower subsequent returns when interest becomes a larger share of the operating and financing cost stack while cash represents a small share of current assets.
considered.reasoning: The change in interest’s cost share captures financing-cost crowd-out rather than a fixed-charge shortfall or interest-to-revenue level. Cash scarcity identifies firms unable to accommodate that reallocation of resources without cutting operations or seeking costly external finance.

critic_notes.rationale: This is the standard operating-profitability anomaly (RMW, which FF5 already prices out) simply restricted to the top-30% leverage subsample, so the conditioning is a sample cut rather than a genuine interaction and the 70% zero mass will make the sorted spread mechanically a "high-leverage profitable vs. everything else" bet.

Operating cash flow scaled by current liabilities is a textbook liquidity/cash-flow-to-debt ratio and a close cousin of published cash-based profitability signals, and despite the "ratio interaction" label it is a single-theme level variable with no cross-theme content beyond choice of denominator.

The expression is internally consistent, but negative-book-equity firms are roughly 2-4% of the cross-section, so ~96% of observations are exactly zero and any long-short spread will be driven by a handful of illiquid micro-caps — precisely the sparse-coverage/unstable-composition artifact the objective warns against.

The double-indicator gate leaves the vast majority of firms at exactly zero, so the sort collapses to a distress dummy that rediscovers the well-documented financial-distress/low-profitability return effect rather than testing an incremental conjunction, and the tied zero leg makes the "long" portfolio essentially arbitrary.

(oancf - ib)/at is simply the negative of total accruals scaled by assets, so this is Sloan's accrual anomaly conditioned on a negative-retained-earnings dummy, and the stated "credible recovery" mechanism is not what the expression distinguishes.

A continuous, full-coverage multiplicative interaction whose sign convention matches the hypothesis and whose components (5-year ROA volatility, leverage) are individually weak-to-known predictors, so the test is genuinely about amplification — though it risks behaving like a simple composite of two known negative signals and should be benchmarked against the additive rank combination to show incremental value.

The SUB(IND_RANK(x), IND_RANK(NEG(x))) construct is just a monotone recentering of the rank of x, so this is structurally the same "signed profitability change × distress rank" design as the archived Leverage-Weighted Profitability Inflection with the inputs swapped for noisier one-period gross-margin and funding-gap deltas — a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

The expression is internally consistent and correctly signed (poor fixed-charge coverage concentrated in short-term-debt-heavy firms), and while the coverage leg overlaps heavily with published distress/interest-coverage anomalies, the refinancing-concentration interaction is a legitimate and testable extension.

Multiplying low operating profitability by low retained earnings/assets is essentially a two-term reconstruction of Altman/Ohlson-style distress plus the RMW profitability factor, so it is a direct rediscovery whose FF5 alpha is likely mechanically absorbed and whose "interaction" adds no information beyond the two well-known levels.

The construction is clean and consistent with the stated sign, and cost rigidity conditioned on a current funding gap is a plausibly novel angle — though SG&A intensity is itself a documented (and oppositely signed, intangible-investment) predictor, so the hypothesis carries real sign risk.

The reasoning openly states it "preserves" the archived Leverage-Weighted Profitability Inflection mechanism, and swapping a 3-period operating-margin trend for a 1-period EBITDA delta and gross debt for net debt is a parameter tweak within the same signal family rather than a substantively different idea.

The R&D × financial-constraint interaction is a published anomaly (Li 2011, RFS) with the opposite documented sign — constrained high-R&D firms earn higher, not lower, returns — and COALESCE(xrd,0) conflates non-reporters with true zeros, creating a large mass point that degrades the industry rank.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's already-tested Interest Rollover Squeeze — the identical (xint − oibdp)/at × dlc/lt structure with dp merely added inside the numerator — so it re-tests an evaluated signal rather than a new mechanism.

Despite the "novel interaction" label this is a single unconditional ratio whose cross-sectional variation will be dominated by −oibdp/at plus a current-liability accrual term, i.e. a mechanical repackaging of the operating-profitability and liability-accrual anomalies rather than a genuine cross-theme construct.

Replacing symmetric profitability volatility with a directional distance-from-peak measure is a substantively different and economically coherent response to the failed vol×leverage signal, and the expression's sign direction matches the stated hypothesis.

The first leg (Δche − oibdp)/at is dominated by negative profitability rather than by "debt-funded liquidity," so the expression does not compute the stated mechanism and the composite largely collapses into low-profitability × debt-issuance, both documented anomalies.

The first leg loads positively on oiadp, so profitable dividend payers score high on a signal expected to predict low returns — an internal sign conflict with the profitability anomaly — and the construction closely echoes the archive's already-tested Operating Profit Leakage Under Deficit.

The earnings-quality-deterioration leg is a different economic channel from the archive's interest-coverage signal and the direction is internally consistent, though it leans on the well-known accrual anomaly and reuses the dlc/lt conditioner, so the incremental novelty is moderate.

This is a mechanical merge of two existing archive signals (Capital Replacement Debt Trap and Capital Burden Cash Depletion) sharing the identical dp−oibdp core, so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism, and the MIN-of-ranks gate mostly re-sorts the same distressed firms.

Non-debt current liabilities as an operating-credit proxy is a genuinely different leverage construct from the archive's financial-debt measures, though both legs share a revenue denominator (so the interaction partly proxies for low-turnover/low-margin firms) and the negative sign sits uneasily with the net-operating-assets anomaly, which implies high operating liabilities forecast *higher* returns.

The two legs are near-mechanically linked — a large oiadp−pi gap depresses pretax and thus net income, which is what drives ΔRE — so this is close to a squared version of the same variable rather than a true conditional, and it is a level→change tweak of the archived Operating Profit Leakage Under Deficit.

The stated rationale about "comparable asset-scaled units" is wrong — NEG(oibdp/at) is a level typically an order of magnitude larger than the annual deltas, so for the large majority of profitable firms the MIN collapses to −ROA and the signal degenerates into the well-known profitability anomaly, while also being a re-parameterization of the archived Borrowed Cash Amid Operating Weakness.

Scale mismatch undermines the construction: operating-profit drawdowns are typically a few percent of assets while che/at ranges to 0.4+, so the composite is dominated by negative cash holdings and largely rediscovers the cash-holdings return premium rather than testing loss-absorption capacity.

TS_SUM of an indicator over three periods is a near-degenerate 0–3 variable (overwhelmingly 3 for the typical firm), so after ranking the product is essentially just NEG(re/at) — a known distress/retained-earnings predictor already used in the archive — and the positive expected sign contradicts the usual finding that low retained earnings signal distress and lower returns.

The second leg is simply inverted gross profitability (Novy-Marx) and the pairing with operating current liabilities is a denominator swap on the archived "Supplier-Credit Margin Squeeze," so it is a cosmetic variant layered on a canonical published anomaly rather than a new mechanism.

Replacing DELTA with the level in the archived "Rollover Cash-Conversion Breakdown" is a one-operator variant, and the level of (oiadp − oancf)/at is essentially the total-accruals anomaly, so the proposal is both a near-rediscovery of an archived signal and of a well-known published effect.

Both legs already appear in the archive (drawdown in "Low-Cash Profit Drawdown," cash depletion in "Capital Burden Cash Depletion"), so this is a single-conditioner substitution within an already-explored pair space, even though the diagnosis that a static cash-level premium drove the earlier FMB/alpha divergence is economically sensible.

The ABS in the denominator makes the ratio non-monotonic in distress — a firm whose interest expense exceeds EBITDA receives the same score as an identically taxed healthy firm — so the expression does not compute the "tax claim relative to available operating surplus" the hypothesis describes, and high txt is more commonly a profitability proxy pointing the opposite way.

Normalizing profit volatility by revenue volatility to isolate cost-structure amplification is a genuine and well-motivated diagnosis of why the generation-0 volatility×leverage signal failed, though a ratio of two three-observation volatilities is statistically fragile and near-zero revenue volatility will drive the tails even after winsorization.

The construction is internally consistent and the interaction is not in the archive, but the first leg is literally the working-capital accrual measure of the Sloan accruals anomaly, so any result will need to be shown to survive controls for accruals and profitability changes individually.

This is the archived "Low-Cash Profit Drawdown" signal with MUL swapped for MIN on the identical two legs — a cosmetic operator variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the MIN of two industry ranks is also highly correlated with the product.

TS_MAX of operating profitability over three years is nearly collinear with the current profitability level, so the signal reduces to low-profitability × low-working-capital, i.e., a repackaging of the published profitability (RMW) and financial-distress effects, and it also overlaps the archived TS_MIN profitability-floor signal.

The current-asset composition leg is a genuine liquidity-quality construct distinct from the cash/at and wcap/at legs already exhausted in the archive, and its interaction with margin compression plausibly targets inventory/receivable impairment, though the composition leg's inverse relation to cash holdings means part of the effect may be a known cash-holdings anomaly.

The cost-stickiness leg is identical to the archived "Rollover Cost Stickiness" signal and the only change is reparameterizing the maturity leg from a level (dlc/lt) to a one-year change (dlc/lct), which is a marginal respecification likely to add noise rather than diagnose why that signal had a strong alpha but a zero Fama-MacBeth slope.

The competing-claims framing (interest coverage by gross profit versus non-debt current liabilities against current assets) is a reasonably distinct construction from the archived supplier-credit and rollover signals, but the gross-profit denominator will invert the ranking for firms with negative or near-zero gross profit — precisely the distressed subset the hypothesis targets — so a scaled-by-assets numerator would be safer.

ACCEL on operating profitability is a genuinely different trajectory construct from the levels, deltas and drawdowns already tested, though the retained-earnings leg reuses the archive's NEG(re/at) conditioner (which already failed once) and second differences of annual accounting ratios are noisy, so expectations should be modest.

This keeps the identical second leg and mechanism of the archived "Dual-Creditor Gross-Profit Squeeze" and only rescales the first leg from a gross-profit denominator to an asset denominator — a legitimate monotonicity fix but essentially a measurement variant rather than a substantively different signal.

The two legs are mechanically entangled (both built on act−che, so low revenue per noncash current asset largely restates a high noncash current-asset share relative to sales), so the "interaction" is close to a monotone transform of one construct, and the underlying content is a rediscovery of the well-known asset-turnover/inventory-and-receivables-intensity effects.
This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Rollover Asset-Productivity Deficit," swapping at→act and lt→lct while preserving the identical mechanism, legs, and expected sign.

Same two legs and same conditioning variable as the archived "Rollover Gross-to-Cash Disconnect" with only SUB replaced by MIN, and the construction fights itself economically because the high-signal tail requires high gross profitability, a documented positive return predictor.

The maturity-extension leg is a genuinely novel conditioning variable and the expected sign matches the expression's direction, but the turnover-change leg (sales growth minus asset growth) is largely a repackaging of the asset-growth/investment anomaly, so any result will need that control.

Clean, internally consistent duration-mismatch construct using two economically distinct current-level variables not previously paired in the archive, though the dlc/(dltt+dlc) denominator is undefined or noisy for near-zero-debt firms and dp/at should be checked against capital-intensity and accrual proxies.

This is essentially the mirror-image corner of the archived "Productivity Recovery with Maturity Extension" (both legs negated, sign flipped), so with rank(-x)=1-rank(x) it is a near-mechanical variant of an already-tested signal rather than a new mechanism.

Internally consistent and a substantive level-to-change reformulation of the archive's strongest interest-rollover mechanism, though it recycles both building blocks and inherits the archive's pattern of weak portfolio evidence for "coordinated repair" composites.

critic_notes.rationale: The second leg, NEG(DELTA((act-che)/at)), is a direct proxy for the Sloan working-capital accruals anomaly, and the overall construction mirrors the archived "Working-Capital Profit Divergence" with signs flipped, so it is largely rediscovery plus a cosmetic reflection.

A trivial level×level product whose first leg is the published SG&A/organizational-capital anomaly and whose sign flip appears reverse-engineered from the archived "Overhead Rigidity Under Liquidity Pressure" failure rather than motivated ex ante.

This is the differenced, sign-flipped mirror of the archived "Capital Consumption Working-Capital Strain," and its positive expected sign on DELTA(wcap/at) directly contradicts the well-documented accruals direction, making the hypothesis internally questionable.

Margin volatility is a genuinely different first leg from the archive's profitability levels and drawdowns and the supplier-credit conditioning is economically coherent, though a 3-observation VOL is noisy and the closely analogous "Debt Amplified Profit Instability" already failed on a similar instability×creditor-claims premise.

This is a mechanical VOL→drawdown swap on the archived "Cash-Light Fixed-Charge Instability" with an identical cash-composition conditioner, and the drawdown-times-low-cash construction was already tested as "Low-Cash Profit Drawdown" (ls_talpha −4.68), so it is a cosmetic recombination of two archive entries rather than a new mechanism.

Replacing the static short-debt share in the archived "Rollover Asset-Productivity Deficit" with a rise above its three-year minimum is a defensible level-versus-event distinction and the expression is sign-consistent, though the deviation-from-min leg is non-negative with heavy mass at zero and the productivity leg still carries most of the archived cross-sectional strength.

The MIN-based conjunction of the two archived "recovery with maturity extension" signals is internally coherent and tests whether joint operating and servicing improvement is required rather than either alone, but it is a fairly mechanical merge whose main risk is that intersecting two already-thin legs erodes coverage and portfolio stability.

The first leg is byte-identical to the archived "Capital Consumption Working-Capital Strain" and only the conditioner is swapped from a wcap level to a wcap drawdown, a substitution the archive has already applied repeatedly (che, act, oiadp), making this a cosmetic variant rather than a new economic channel.

Because txt/at is an order of magnitude smaller and less dispersed than (oibdp−xint)/at, the "tax shortfall" leg is arithmetically dominated by negative after-interest profitability, so the signal collapses into the well-known profitability anomaly conditioned on low cash — a space the archive already covers via "Worst-Case Fixed-Charge Liquidity Gap" and "Cash-Light Fixed-Charge Instability."

This is the same VOL→drawdown substitution applied to the archived "Supplier-Financed Margin Instability" with an unchanged supplier-claims conditioner, and the drawdown leg is close to a multi-year version of the margin-decline term already used in "Supplier Arrears Margin Compression," so it is an incremental respecification of tested ground.

This is the archived "Cash-Light Fixed-Charge Instability" (identical volatility and cash-share legs, ls_talpha −3.60) with a MIN gate on dlc/lt bolted on — the same dlc/lt gate already paired with volatility terms in "Rollover Nonoperating-Charge Instability" — so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism.

The three components are all previously tested individually, but replacing the profitability level in "Operating Loss Current-Asset Drawdown" with a binding MIN of two economically distinct deficiencies (operating scale vs. debt service) changes the conditioning content rather than just adding a filter, and the sign logic is internally consistent.

This is "Three-Way Refinancing Rehabilitation" with the asset-productivity leg swapped for cash-share growth — same MIN(fixed-charge improvement, maturity extension) core and same composite logic — a one-variable substitution on an already-evaluated signal.

The margin × supplier-claims core duplicates the archived "Supplier-Credit Margin Squeeze"/"Dual-Creditor Gross-Profit Squeeze" pair with only a denominator change (revt→act) plus the recycled current-asset drawdown gate, and the standalone cogs/revt leg is essentially inverse gross profitability, a well-known anomaly.

Identical to the archived "Capital Consumption Working-Capital Strain" (same dp−gross-profit burden and NEG(wcap/at) legs, ls_talpha −3.71) except for a MIN with the heavily reused dlc/lt gate, which is a refinement of an existing result rather than a distinct hypothesis.

This appends the same current-asset drawdown gate to the archived "Supplier Credit Withdrawal During Operating Decline"; the disambiguation argument (withdrawal vs. voluntary repayment) is reasonable but the act-drawdown and Δ(lct−dlc)/at legs are partly mechanically linked through the shrinking balance sheet, so the added gate risks reinforcing rather than conditioning the original signal.
